html:
The County of Toulouse was a large feudal state in southern France, in the Languedoc, from Carolingian times to 1271. It is on the map for 1200.

Its counts ruled from Toulouse over a land where people spoke Occitan, troubadours wrote love poetry, and the French king's power hardly reached. Count Raymond IV was one of the leaders of the First Crusade, which took Jerusalem in 1099; see First Crusade takes Jerusalem.

Around 1200 the county was a stronghold of the Cathars, Christians who rejected the Catholic church. In 1209 the pope launched the Albigensian Crusade against them. Northern French knights under Simon de Montfort beat the count and his ally the king of Aragon at Muret in 1213. The war ended in 1229 with the county bound to the French crown, and in 1271 it passed fully to France.
sum: The County of Toulouse was a large feudal state in southern France, in the Languedoc, from Carolingian times to 1271. It is on the map for 1200.
